rationale: Resolve the next-discriminator contract before introducing a snapshot/application obligation. Newly acquired usage documentation and the snapshot transfer test distinguish local work completion from state-machine ordering.

feedback.answered: The asynchronous usage contract expressly replaces regular Ready persistence/application fields and Advance with local messages, preserves FIFO per target, and permits arbitrary order across append and apply targets. Its append example saves the snapshot and sends attached responses; its apply example processes committed entries and configuration calls. In the implementation, restoring a snapshot installs its configuration before local completion. MsgStorageApplyResp advances applied progress through max(old,index), but does not clear the unstable snapshot. appliedSnap separately clears only the matching snapshot index and advances application progress. promotable checks the presence of any pending or in-progress snapshot, not merely applied index. Thus source inspection identifies a specific barrier against an older application response enabling a campaign. The captured transfer test independently expects snapshot processing before a successful transfer response, but uses internal setup and does not execute the proposed asynchronous history. No new execution or property outcome is asserted.
remaining: The asynchronous documentation does not explicitly explain how application state-machine snapshot installation is serialized against an older committed configuration batch already handed to the apply target. Cross-target permission alone is insufficient to attribute stale configuration application to a legal caller history.

The narrower pending-snapshot election barrier needs a producer-derived history: a real lagging follower with older normal-entry apply work outstanding, an automatically produced snapshot from a compacted leader, and campaign attempts before and after the actual snapshot completion.
Multiple replacement snapshots, stale-term snapshot completion and client/application endpoints remain distinct questions.
feedback.rationale: Select the single-snapshot/older-normal-apply discriminator next. It isolates the authority barrier without depending on the unresolved ordering of configuration application and state-machine snapshot installation. Construct it using actual proposal, commit, CreateSnapshot, compaction and replication paths, preserve per-target FIFO, complete old normal application before installing the snapshot, and compare explicit Campaign effects while snapshot append completion is held versus released. First preserve its pending-snapshot lifecycle in the shared map before a formal Candidate relies on it. The wider stale-configuration hypothesis remains a contract question, not a finding.
